newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Greenfields says Canada bid is too low.
newsitem.headline: Greenfields says Canada bid is too low.

text.p: Greenfields Coal Co Ltd, which is developing a coal recovery plant in the United States, said on Friday that a share-swap takeover offer by Mineral Resources Corp (MRC) of Canada was not welcome.

"On the information available to the directors to date, the offer by MRC appears to grossly undervalue the inherent value of Greenfield's shares," it said, adding that a recommended bid would have to consist of a cash offer in excess of 35 cents.

"The directors current view is that the offer received from MRC should be vigorously defended and the offer should be regarded as a hostile and opportunistic takeover bid at a significant discount to net present value."

MRC said it would offer one of its shares for every eight Greenfields shares, which were trading at 14 cents at 2.40 p.m. (0440 GMT). Greenfields has a market capitalisation of A$14.2 million based on 101.65 million shares on issue. Its stock has reached a high of 40 cents in 1997 and a low of 12.5 cents.
MRC shares ended at C$0.86 on Thursday, valuing each Greenfields share at 10.75 cents.
Greenfields owns the Alpheus coal reclamation plant in West Virgini, which has contracts to supply US Steel and has forecast annual output of 240,000 tons of clean coal.
MRC said it was the largest shareholder in Greenfields with an 18 percent stake and disagreed with the Australian company's business plan, including capital raising projects.
